newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday were inactive, with no trades, feedlot sources said.
Owners were pricing cattle at $65.00 to mostly $66.00, but no packer bids were noted as packers take inventory of feedlot showlists, the sources said.
Once bids do surface, they are expected at $63.00 to $64.00, they said. Sales last week were rather hefty at $64.00, which was up $2.00 from the previous week.
Fed cattle prices were underpinned by strong CME live cattle futures and firm beef values, they said.
Strength in fed cattle prices also was expected to continue amid outlooks for declines in market-ready cattle supplies into the fall, the feedlot sources said.
If fed cattle prices trade at $65.00 this week, it would bring most owners close to break-even on their costs, the sources said.
At last week's level of $64.00, several feedlots reported owners were losing an average of $10.00 to $15.00 per head.
